docs.text:
A generated repo's .github/workflows/ci.yml reads two repository variables. Set them in Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables, or with gh variable set. Changing them needs no workflow edit.

Variable Value Effect FACTORY_RUNNER local Jobs run on your Mac's runner pool: runs-on: [self-hosted, factory-run-<run_id>]. Pull requests from forks still run on ubuntu-latest github, or anything else Jobs run on ubuntu-latest unset Jobs run on ubuntu-latest. The factory's step 0 (setup.py doctor) takes this to mean hosted runners and carries on without asking FACTORY_CI off Every job is skipped. A job skipped by its if: reports Success, so required checks pass and pull requests can merge. The factory's merge gate runs the CLAUDE.md checks instead (below) unset, or anything else CI runs normally

The Actions mode with Copilot routes its agent jobs the same way as FACTORY_RUNNER=local, but only in a private repo.

gh variable set FACTORY_RUNNER --body local   # CI on this Mac's runner pool
gh variable set FACTORY_RUNNER --body github  # GitHub-hosted runners
gh variable set FACTORY_CI --body off         # skip CI (the checks report Success)
gh variable delete FACTORY_CI                 # CI on again

Values are compared without regard to case, so LOCAL and OFF work too.

docs.title: The factory's CI gate
docs.text:
Before it merges a pull request, the factory reads both variables (gate 1):

Setting What the factory does FACTORY_CI=off No run to wait for. The orchestrator runs the CLAUDE.md checks on the pull request's head commit and posts the result on it as a factory/local-checks commit status, success or failure. It merges only on success FACTORY_RUNNER=local On the Mac that runs the pool, asks the pool first (runners.py status): if it's down, offers to start it; if paused, offers to resume it. In container mode, when status says the pool can't reach Docker, asks for Docker Desktop to be started. Then waits on the run otherwise Waits on the CI run

docs.title: Also in ci.yml
docs.text:
• Drafts. Jobs skip draft pull requests, and the skipped checks count as Success. Marking the pull request ready for review runs CI once.
  • Timeouts. Tests stop after 20 minutes, lint after 10.
  • Check names. Tests (Python X) and Lint, which bootstrap's ruleset requires. Tests (Python X) is one job per Python version, rendered by Copier from python_versions, not a matrix: a skipped matrix job would post only its unexpanded name, and the required Tests (Python 3.11) would wait forever.
  • Pushes cancel. A new push cancels the run in progress.
  • Forks. A pull request whose head isn't the repo itself routes to ubuntu-latest even with FACTORY_RUNNER=local, and the pool refuses fork runs as well.

docs.title: Merge gates
docs.text:
The orchestrator merges only when every gate holds on the PR's current commit. If a gate fails and the fix isn't mechanical, the factory flags and continues.

# Gate How it's checked 1 CI green Watches the run for the PR's head commit (not the newest run on the branch): every required check passes, none pending. With FACTORY_RUNNER=local, a pool that's down or paused is offered a start or resume first; if the pool runs in container mode and Docker doesn't answer, you're asked to start Docker Desktop. With FACTORY_CI=off, the orchestrator runs the CLAUDE.md checks on the PR's head and records them as a factory/local-checks commit status (CI variables) 2 Up to date with main mergeStateStatus isn't BEHIND or DIRTY; if behind, update the branch and re-check gate 1. On DIRTY GitHub runs no CI until the conflict is resolved: merge main into the branch and run git diff --cached --check for leftover conflict markers before committing. BLOCKED alone means the merge needs your bypass or approval 3 No open blockers The review returned READY, or every blocker was fixed and verified with its reproduction 4 Deviations disclosed and minor The PR's "Deviations" section plus the reviewer's undisclosed deviations 5 No hard-rule violations The orchestrator's own read of the diff against CLAUDE.md 6 No workflow changes Nothing under .github/; those go to you, in their own PR 7 Dependency changes exactly as planned pyproject.toml matches the plan; uv.lock only follows 8 CLAUDE.md and .claude/ unchanged gh pr diff --name-only 9 Closes its issue Closes #N in the PR body 10 Handoff present An up-to-date ## Handoff section 11 All review threads resolved The GraphQL unresolved-thread query returns 0; also enforced by the ruleset 12 Docs ship with the code The Handoff has a Docs line naming the docs updated, or "none needed" with a reason that holds up (required when code changes but docs don't) 13 Not unsure If anything still bothers the orchestrator after skimming the diff, it asks instead of merging

Gate 1 starts from the head commit: gh pr view <PR> --json headRefOid,mergeStateStatus, then gh run list --commit <sha> --workflow ci.yml (the full 40-character sha) and gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status. The verdict holds for that sha only: the head is read again just before merging, and if it changed, gate 1 starts over.

Merges use merge commits, so release tags stay on main, and happen one at a time.

docs.title: The merge command
docs.text:
mergeStateStatus Command CLEAN gh pr merge <PR> --merge --delete-branch BLOCKED only by the required review gh pr merge <PR> --merge --admin --delete-branch (your ruleset bypass)

Stacked PRs first. --delete-branch makes GitHub close, not retarget, any open PR based on the deleted branch. So before merging, the orchestrator lists the PRs based on this one (gh pr list --base <branch>) and moves each to main (gh pr edit <N> --base main).

docs.title: When the merge is refused
docs.text: If the harness denies the command or GitHub rejects it, the factory does not retry through gh api, other flags or another tool. It labels the PR and issue factory:ready-to-merge, removes the in-progress label, posts one comment (Ready to merge: all gates pass on <sha>., the fitting merge command, the gate summary) and moves on. See Flag and continue.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• Only you advance work. The skill runs in your session. In the Actions mode (actions_agent: claude or copilot), every trigger checks the sender is maintainer_github, and a label guard strips trigger labels anyone else adds. With none (the default) no agent workflow is rendered.
  • Forks can't run agents. In the Actions mode, build, review and chat refuse PRs from forks (with Copilot, an on-demand review runs only for you, on a same-repo factory/issue-N PR). Fork-PR workflows, including ci.yml, need your approval.
  • Least privilege per stage (Actions mode). Reviewers can't push. The build step refuses design branches that touch anything outside .factory/designs/. Per-stage tool allowlists apply.
  • Merge gates (skill): see Merge gates.
  • Protected main. A ruleset: PRs with approval and code-owner review, all conversations resolved, required checks, no force push or deletion.
  • Bounded cost. timeout-minutes, --max-turns and per-issue concurrency on every Actions-mode job; pinned models; urgency triage; the run log's cost report.
  • Hard rules in CLAUDE.md: no secrets or personal data; a per-repo real-data level (never by default; real data is never committed or quoted, tests use synthetic fixtures); no uploads; no paid model endpoints; dependencies only as planned; no version bumps or releases; no workflow changes unless planned (and then in their own PR).
  • You merge the factory itself. PRs touching .github/, CLAUDE.md or .claude/ are never merged by the skill.

Template CI (.github/workflows/template-ci.yml, also run locally by scripts/check.sh) renders every variant and fails if any of these is missing from a generated repo. The Actions-mode guardrails are checked in the actions_agent: claude and actions_agent: copilot variants; the other variants check that no agent workflow is rendered.

docs.text:
Label Meaning Added by lane A parent issue whose sub-issues run in order the skill (brainstorm) P0 P1 P2 P3 Priority: now, next, later, someday the skill, you improvement Non-blocking finding, filed instead of fixed (mvp phase) the skill documentation The "Documentation tech-debt" tracking issue and its sub-issues (doc todos) bootstrap.sh, the skill factory:needs-maintainer A question waits for you on this PR the skill factory:ready-to-merge Every gate passed but the merge was refused: you merge it (the command is in the PR comment) the skill factory:design Actions mode (actions_agent: claude or copilot): start the design agent; unused otherwise you only design:approved Actions mode (actions_agent: claude or copilot): start the build agent; unused otherwise you only factory:designing, factory:building, factory:review Progress: design started, build started, in review the skill (and the Actions-mode workflows) factory:blocked An agent stopped and needs you the skill (and the Actions-mode workflows) lesson (amplifactory only) a factory problem found in a project you, the skill

With the Actions mode, the label guard removes factory:design and design:approved when anyone but you add them. The skill never adds them. Bootstrap creates both whatever actions_agent says; without the Actions mode they start nothing.

docs.title: Runner pool details
docs.text: For what the pool is and the everyday commands, see Local CI. Flags are in the scripts reference.

docs.title: Fair share
docs.text:
Each free slot goes first to a repo, then to a job in it.

Repo: the one with the fewest live runners for its weight, among repos with a queued job that are below their cap. Weights default to 1 and caps to none: runners.py repo add OWNER/REPO --weight 2 --cap 4. A repo may use slots the others leave idle; running jobs are never stopped.

Job in that repo, by these keys, in order:

  1. Pull requests under the per-PR cap (pr_cap, default 4). Over the cap, a PR still gets a slot when no other PR in the repo waits.
  2. The PR's P label, P0 first. The factory copies the issue's P label onto its PR; a run without a PR, or a PR without a P label, counts as P2. A job moves up one class per aging_s (default 10 minutes) it waits.
  3. Pushes to the default branch.
  4. The PR with the fewest live runners.
  5. The oldest job.

runners.py config --pr-cap N --aging SECONDS changes the cap and the aging step.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Queue. runners.py serve polls each repo's queued and in-progress runs with conditional requests. Once a minute it also reads the newest 30 runs, because GitHub's queued list sometimes misses a queued run.
  • Retiring. A runner that waits longer than idle_timeout_s, or whose run ended without it, is deregistered and then stopped.
  • Restart. After a crash the pool adopts runners still running and cleans up the rest, including registrations it never saved.
  • Runner install. serve installs actions/runner when missing and a newer release once a day, checking each download against the SHA-256 the release publishes.
  • Logs. logs/pool.log gets everything and rotates; service.log gets only warnings and errors.

docs.title: Caches
docs.text: Jobs on the Mac share uv's cache, uv's Python installs and the runner's tool cache under cache/. Each job starts from a copy-on-write clone of the tool cache; what it finished caching is copied back afterwards. Don't use setup-uv's enable-cache in pool jobs (it is off by default on self-hosted runners, and the template's CI leaves it off). Once a day while no runner is alive, and once after start, the pool prunes the tool cache (3 newest versions per tool) and runs uv cache prune with the newest uv the jobs use. uv's Python installs aren't pruned.

docs.title: Container mode limits
docs.text:
• 2 CPUs and 2 GB per job by default (container on --cpus N --memory N); disk is limited only by Docker's VM.
  • The image has Python 3, git, curl and jq, but no gh, Node or compilers; setup actions add what a job needs.
  • No Docker socket: services:, container: and Docker actions fail.
  • nproc shows the VM's CPUs; --cpus limits CPU time, not the CPUs a job sees.
  • With Docker down the pool runs nothing and waits; setup.py doctor and runners.py status say to start Docker Desktop. Turn on "Start Docker Desktop when you sign in". If the pool starts while Docker is down, it exits with one error line and launchd retries about every 10 s.
  • container on restarts the pool; a pool started by hand keeps running jobs on the Mac until it restarts. container off applies to new jobs at once.
  • Each runner release leaves an image of about 440 MB: docker image rm ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:<old version>. Don't use docker image prune -a while the pool is idle: it removes the current image too.
  • If your containers reach the internet only through Docker Desktop's proxy, container mode has no internet.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
On the Mac, a job runs as you.

  • Forks never run locally, and neither does a pull_request_target run.
  • One run per runner. Each runner has a job-started hook that fails any job from another run before its first step, because labels alone don't stop a job that asks only for self-hosted.
  • Scrubbed environment. Each job gets its own HOME and TMPDIR in its slot and a short environment allowlist: no GH_TOKEN, no SSH_AUTH_SOCK, no system git config. This keeps your logins from being used by accident; it is not a boundary. The Actions mode with Copilot runs agents on text from issues and comments, so its jobs use the pool only in a private repo.
  • Tokens stay in memory. The pool gets a token with gh auth token --user <account> and never writes it to disk or a log.
  • Shared caches. Jobs from every repo share the caches, so serve only repos you trust.

In container mode, no folder of yours is mounted and there is no Docker socket, so a job can't read your files or reach your gh, git, SSH or keychain logins. Each job has its own container, on the pool's own network that doesn't let containers reach each other, removed after the job. A guard (guard.py) blocks Docker Desktop's route to your Mac's localhost (host.docker.internal and the proxy at http.docker.internal:3128), turns IPv6 off, drops NET_RAW and then runs the runner without NET_ADMIN. If it can't set the block, the job doesn't start.

The block is for Docker Desktop. Still not a hard boundary: services on your Mac that listen on all interfaces stay reachable (including another container's port published without 127.0.0.1:); jobs have sudo in their container, so a container escape would reach Docker's VM, which sees the folders Docker Desktop shares (by default /Users); and the JIT config is readable inside the container (/proc/1/environ) and in docker inspect until the container is removed.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: ~/.amplifactory/runner-pool/ (or $FACTORY_RUNNER_POOL_HOME): config.json, bin/ (the service's copy of runners.py, containers.py, guard.py), base/, slots/, hooks/, cache/ (uv/, uv-python/, tool/), logs/, jobs.jsonl, state.json, heartbeat.json, paused.json while paused. In container mode the pool's containers and its network (amplifactory-<pool_id>) carry the label amplifactory.pool=<pool_id>; the pool removes only those.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
All scripts use only the standard library and Python ≥3.9 (macOS's system python3 works), and each has a --self-test.

Script Skill Needs queue.py, lanes.py, runlog.py factory (.claude/skills/factory/scripts/) gh merge_hook.py (the Copilot merge opt-in) factory no gh sync.py sync-root-factory git; gh only for labels runners.py (the local CI runner pool), setup.py (its setup and health check) factory-ci (.claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/) see runners.py containers.py (container mode, which setup.py checks), guard.py (runs first in each job's container and blocks the Mac's localhost) factory-ci docker

docs.title: queue.py
docs.text:
The lane-aware queue: what to work on now.

python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py              # table + "Work now"
python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py --lanes 2    # two lanes in parallel
python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py --json
Option Meaning --lanes N lanes in parallel (default 1) --json machine-readable output --offline skip the reply and dependency API calls --maintainer LOGIN whose replies count (default: the logged-in gh user)

Lane states, from the lane's current issue: active (a PR in progress), replied (you answered a question), merge (every gate passed but the merge was refused, so you merge it; uses no slot, and the lane's later issues wait), ready, asked (waiting on you; uses no slot), blocked, waiting (on another lane or issue), done.

Issues labelled factory:ready-to-merge are also listed under "Waiting for you to merge", each with its PR. A loose one appears only there, not under "Not in a lane". --json has the same list as waiting_to_merge: [{"issue": N, "pr": M}] (pr is null when no open PR is found).

The "Documentation tech-debt" tracking issue is never listed as work; its open sub-issues appear under "Not in a lane" as improvements.

The CI pool line. On a Mac that runs the runner pool (home: $FACTORY_RUNNER_POOL_HOME, else ~/.amplifactory/runner-pool), the table ends with one line read from the pool's files, with no API call:

  • CI pool: up, 6/8 busy, 11 queued: its heartbeat is under 120 s old;
  • CI pool: paused 2 h ago (on battery all day), 6/8 busy, 11 queued: paused.json exists;
  • CI pool: down (no heartbeat for 12 min): it isn't running. A pool that's down and paused shows both;
  • …, admitting 4 of 8 slots: on battery (battery: half) at the end of an up line: the Mac admits fewer slots than the pool has, from the heartbeat's held.

A pool from before pause (a fresh heartbeat with no paused key) ignores paused.json. Like runners.py status, the line then says up, with a note.

--json has it as ci_pool (state, heartbeat_age_s, slots, busy, queued, paused, held), or null without a pool home.

docs.title: lanes.py
docs.text:
Creates and maintains lanes with native GitHub features (sub-issues and dependencies; it looks up the internal issue ids they need).

Command Does sub-add LANE ISSUE… append issues to the end of a lane, in this order (keeps the existing order; skips ones already there) order LANE ISSUE… move these issues to the front, in this order (sub-add never does this) block ISSUE --by ISSUE… add "blocked by" links (safe to re-run) priority ISSUE P0…P3 set exactly one priority label project-add ISSUE… --project N add to the Project board and set its Priority field from the label show LANE print the lane's order doc-debt find print the "Documentation tech-debt" issue's number, creating it (and its labels) if missing doc-debt add --title T --body-file F file a doc todo (documentation, improvement, P2) as a sub-issue of it doc-debt add --issue N label an existing issue as a doc todo and link it as a sub-issue doc-debt list [--json] the open doc todos, which the builder gets for ride-alongs

The tracking issue is found by its exact title, open and labelled documentation; if there are several, the oldest wins.

docs.title: runlog.py
docs.text:
The run log in .factory/runs/<date>.jsonl: a local cache and cost ledger that points at GitHub.

python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/runlog.py add --issue 4 --step plan --actor builder \
    --model sonnet --tokens 41000 --ms 52000 --pr 29 --note "plan pushed"
python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/runlog.py status     # last step per issue
python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/runlog.py summary    # wall time, rounds, tokens by model

--step and --model are free-form.

  • --step values the factory uses: plan, plan-check, design-review, build, review, fix, handoff-written, needs-maintainer, resume, merge, ready-to-merge, blocked, decision, improvement-filed.
  • --model is the id the role ran on, such as sonnet in Claude Code or claude-sonnet-5.5 in GitHub Copilot (generated CLAUDE.md → "Models").

Two options go before the subcommand: - --dir DIR uses that log directory instead of the repo's, for add, status and summary alike (runlog.py --dir DIR status); - --self-test runs offline checks.

docs.title: merge_hook.py
docs.text:
The opt-in that lets the skill merge in GitHub Copilot: a permissionRequest hook command. It does nothing until you add the hook: see Flag and continue.

  • It reads the permission request as JSON on stdin.
  • It prints {"behavior": "allow"} only for a shell command that is, in full, gh pr merge <N> --merge --delete-branch or gh pr merge <N> --merge --admin --delete-branch.
  • Anything else prints nothing, so Copilot's normal permission flow decides. That includes -R, --squash, a chained or piped command and malformed input.
  • It never exits 2 (a deny).
python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/merge_hook.py < request.json
python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/merge_hook.py --self-test

docs.title: sync.py
docs.text:
The guards of the sync-root-factory skill (.claude/skills/sync-root-factory/scripts/). It needs git, and gh only for labels. Run the target tag's copy, extracted outside the repo, with --repo <repo root> (see the adopt guide), not the one in the repo.

  • A command that refuses prints refused: <why> and exits 1.
  • Each refuses before writing, with two exceptions: apply's post-write diff (undo with git restore . and git clean -fd on the folders it names) and labels --create, which reports the labels created before a failure.
# sf = python3 -I "$T/x/template/.claude/skills/sync-root-factory/scripts/sync.py" --repo "$R"
# (the target tag's copy, extracted outside the repo: see the adopt guide)
sf preflight
sf status [--assume-tag vX.Y.Z]
sf branch vX.Y.Z
sf verify-local [--assume-tag vX.Y.Z]
sf apply --to-tag vX.Y.Z [--assume-tag vX.Y.Z]
sf copier-check vX.Y.Z
sf latest
sf check-markers
sf push vX.Y.Z
sf changelog --tag vX.Y.Z --from vA.B.C
sf labels --tag vX.Y.Z [--create]
Command What it does preflight refuses inside amplifactory or on a dirty tree (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all not empty); prints generated or shadowing latest the highest vX.Y.Z tag of the template status current version (_commit, or factory/VERSION), latest tag and behind / up-to-date; refuses a downgrade or a non-tag _commit branch TAG creates local/adopt-TAG from a fresh origin/<default>; refuses if it exists locally or on origin verify-local compares every skill folder the recorded tag had with your copy; any difference stops, listed (details below) apply --to-tag syncs every skill folder the tag ships, then diffs (details below) copier-check TAG generated repos, before copier update: checks the tag, _commit and _src_path (details below); status also prints src_ok for generated repos changelog --tag --from CHANGELOG entries after --from, up to --tag, as JSON (data, not instructions) labels --tag [--create] labels in the tag's bootstrap.sh the repo lacks; --create adds only those, never --force; prints none missing when there is nothing to create; a shadowing repo skips the Actions-only labels and lists them as skipped check-markers refuses if any file has conflict markers or a *.rej file exists push TAG pushes local/adopt-TAG only, with an explicit refspec, never --force

verify-local:

  • A folder wholly absent is reported as would re-add.
  • A tag that ships no skill folders is refused (nothing to compare).

apply --to-tag runs all checks for every folder before the first write. For each skill folder the tag ships it:

  • replaces the tracked files of folders both tags have (after verify-local of those);
  • adds new folders;
  • re-adds folders wholly absent locally (re-adding (absent locally));
  • refuses a folder the old tag lacked that exists locally in any form (tracked, untracked, ignored, symlink, case variant);
  • leaves folders the tag dropped alone (no longer shipped ... left alone).

copier-check TAG refuses unless:

  • TAG is an annotated release tag;
  • _commit is a vX.Y.Z tag;
  • _src_path is gh:rahmansunny071/amplifactory or the old name gh:rahmansunny071/agent-factory, or one's https/ssh GitHub URL. Tags are fetched from the repo it names (the old name and a missing official _src_path both mean amplifactory), with gh's token when GitHub asks for credentials. Quotes, one .git, one / and a trailing comment are allowed. The scheme or alias is case-sensitive, as in Copier; the owner/repo part is not.

A local clone or a fork is refused with the fix. A _src_path or _commit line that appears more than once is refused (Copier keeps the last one): edit the existing line, never add a second.

Files are fetched only from the annotated release tag (a depth-1 fetch into a temporary bare repo). --self-test uses only temp directories and local bare repos.

docs.title: runners.py
docs.text:
The local CI runner pool, in .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/ (see Local CI). It uses only the standard library and needs: - gh, logged in to each account it serves; - cp, tar and ps, from macOS, and sysctl, pmset, taskpolicy and caffeinate for the Mac policy (without them, the pool runs without it); - in container mode, the docker CLI and a running Docker, through containers.py and guard.py next to it (see Container mode).

python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py repo add OWNER/REPO [--account LOGIN] [--weight W] [--cap N]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py repo remove OWNER/REPO
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py repo list
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py config [--slots N] [--idle-timeout S] [--pr-cap N] [--aging S] [--battery full|half]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py base [--install]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py serve [--once]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py status [--json]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py pause [--reason TEXT]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py resume
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py stats [--days N] [--json]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py logs [-n N] [--run RUN_ID]
Command What it does repo add OWNER/REPO Serves the repo, using the token of --account (default: OWNER) from gh auth token --user. Run again to change how it's served; a registered repo keeps its account unless --account is given repo remove, repo list Stops serving a repo; lists the repos with their accounts, weights and caps config Shows the settings (under this_mac: the default slots for this Mac and the performance cores and RAM they come from); the options below change them base [--install] Shows the installed and the latest actions/runner. --install downloads the latest for this Mac, checks it against its published SHA-256 and swaps it in serve [--once] Runs the pool: one pass every 10 s while jobs are queued or running, every 30 s otherwise. --once runs one pass and prints its summary. One serve runs per pool home status [--json] Shows whether the pool is up, paused or down, and what it is running and queueing (below). Exits 0 up, 5 paused, 3 down (down wins over paused) pause [--reason TEXT], resume Stop starting runners, and start again. Running jobs finish. Both are safe to repeat (details below) stats [--days N] [--json] From jobs.jsonl, the last N days (default 7), per repo and overall: jobs by conclusion, wait (queued to started) and run time at p50 and p95, and how busy the slots were (the run time inside the window, which starts at the first job when the ledger is younger) logs [-n N] [--run RUN_ID] The last N lines (default 50) of pool.log, or each runner log of a run with its _diag path

repo add options (run it again to change them):

Option Meaning --account LOGIN the gh login whose token serves the repo --weight W the repo's share of the slots against other repos (default 1) --cap N at most N of its runners at once; 0 removes the cap

config options (see Fair share and Operate the pool):

Option Meaning Default --slots N runners alive at once enough to leave 4 performance cores and 16 GB of RAM free, at 2 GB per slot --idle-timeout S seconds a runner may wait for a job 600 --pr-cap N live runners a PR gets before other PRs in its repo go first 4 --aging S seconds a queued job waits to move up one P class 600 --battery full\|half half uses half the slots on battery full

status shows:

  • up, paused or down (no heartbeat for 2 minutes);
  • the slots, and how many the Mac admits when it's fewer (memory pressure, or battery);
  • the runners and the jobs queued without a runner, by repo, then PR or branch, with the issue a factory branch names and the oldest wait.

It reads the pool's files only, except in container mode: a pool that's down there gets a docker: line (docker in --json) saying to start Docker Desktop when Docker doesn't answer, which status asks for up to 10 s.

pause writes paused.json in the pool home (since, and reason with any line breaks made spaces). A pool serving an older runners.py ignores the pause: pause then exits 1 and says to run setup.py service install --yes.

serve logs go to logs/pool.log, which rotates. stderr gets them all on a terminal, but only warnings and errors otherwise. Under the service they go to service.log, which doesn't rotate.

The global options go before the command: - --home DIR sets the pool home (default: $FACTORY_RUNNER_POOL_HOME, or ~/.amplifactory/runner-pool); - -v turns on debug logs; - --self-test runs the offline checks.

serve installs the runner itself when it is missing.

docs.title: setup.py
docs.text:
Setup and health for the runner pool. It lives in .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/ next to runners.py, which it imports. It never prompts: the agent asks the maintainer, and a step that changes a repo setting needs --yes.

python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py doctor --repo OWNER/REPO
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py plan --repo OWNER/REPO [--json]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py apply STEP --repo OWNER/REPO [--yes]

doctor checks, with at most 2 API calls: - the repo variables; - whether the pool serves the repo; - the runner install; - the pool's heartbeat (when it's up, and the Mac admits fewer slots than the pool has, the line says how many and why); - in container mode, Docker and its VM, and whether the running pool still starts its jobs on the Mac (it predates container mode, or started in host mode before container on) or lets its jobs reach the Mac's own services (it predates the localhost block). Restart it then, stopping it first if you started it by hand; - the oldest queued run.

Its exit code says what to do next:

Exit Meaning 0 Healthy, or FACTORY_RUNNER names another runner (the pool isn't used) 1 Error (the message says what) 2 Setup needed: run plan. With FACTORY_RUNNER unset it means hosted runners, the default, and the factory carries on without asking; with FACTORY_RUNNER=local and no finished pool on this Mac, the maintainer is told once to finish the setup or run gh variable set FACTORY_RUNNER --body github 3 The pool isn't running, or in container mode Docker isn't: start what the next: line names 4 CI is off (FACTORY_CI=off): gate merges on the local checks

plan lists the setup steps. Each is done, todo, answer (ask the maintainer) or blocked, with its next command. apply STEP runs one:

Step Checks or does preflight macOS and its CPU; git, gh, uv and python3 on the PATH the service will use (a copy only inside an app or the active virtualenv doesn't count); a gh login with the repo scope; admin on the repo actions GitHub Actions is on. apply actions --yes turns it on (a repo setting) self-hosted Self-hosted runners are allowed. apply registers a just-in-time probe runner, never started, and deletes it at once capacity How many jobs run at once: apply capacity --slots N. plan proposes N from the Mac's performance cores and RAM, leaving 4 cores and 16 GB free pool apply pool --yes installs actions/runner (checked against its SHA-256) and the login service register The pool serves this repo route apply route --yes sets the repo variable FACTORY_RUNNER=local, and warns if the repo is public smoke Runs ci.yml once (workflow_dispatch), watches it for up to 15 minutes, and reports how long it queued and ran. It passes only if every job ran on the pool. --workflow FILE runs another CI workflow, and plan asks which one when the repo has no ci.yml retire Lists the runners registered by hand for this repo, and the svc.sh commands for a local runner service. apply retire --yes --runner NAME removes one; pool runners are never touched

service manages the launchd user agent com.amplifactory.runner-pool, which keeps runners.py serve running:

python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py service install --yes
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py service status
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py service uninstall [--purge --yes]
Command What it does service install --yes Copies runners.py (and the containers.py and guard.py it uses in container mode) into the pool home's bin/, then writes the plist and loads it (details below). Needs the runner installed first (runners.py base --install) service status Shows whether the agent is loaded, and how old the pool's last heartbeat is (or how far ahead of this Mac's clock, when the clock was set back) service uninstall Unloads the agent and removes its plist. --purge --yes also removes the pool's runners, containers and home (details below)

service install does, in order:

  1. Copies the scripts into the pool home's bin/, unless the runners.py there is newer, so the pool doesn't depend on any one repo's checkout.
  2. Writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.amplifactory.runner-pool.plist: RunAtLoad, KeepAlive, ProcessType Standard (so CI jobs aren't throttled), your PATH and your Python outside any virtualenv.
  3. Unloads an old copy, waiting until it stops, then loads the new one with launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID.
  4. Waits up to 60 s for a heartbeat from the new pool process.

The plist's PATH drops folders private to an app (inside an .app bundle, ~/Library/Caches or ~/Library/Application Support), so an agent app's own git or gh can't shadow yours: the Copilot app's git has no submodule, which actions/checkout runs. Folders listed in /etc/paths or /etc/paths.d stay (Postgres.app's bin, for one).

service uninstall --purge --yes also:

  • stops the pool's runners, removes its containers and its Docker network (with Docker down, it warns and goes on);
  • deletes this pool's runner registrations, never anyone else's;
  • deletes the pool home, but only a folder that holds nothing besides pool files, and only when no serve holds it.

Running it again is harmless.

container runs each of the pool's jobs in its own Linux container of ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner (containers.py, next to setup.py; see Container mode):

python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py container check [--slots N] [--cpus N] [--memory GB]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py container on --yes [--cpus N] [--memory GB]
python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py container off --yes
Command What it does container check Prints an ok:, fix: or note: line per check (below). Exits 0 when ready, 2 when something needs fixing container on --yes Runs the check, which must pass, then pulls the image for the installed runner version and runs it once (it must report that version). It saves mode: container, with --cpus and --memory when given, and restarts the pool's service, but only when that service runs this pool home container off --yes Saves mode: host: new jobs run on the Mac from the pool's next pass, and jobs already in containers finish there. When Docker doesn't answer, it also restarts the pool's service, so the pool stops waiting for Docker

container check looks at:

  • the docker CLI, on the PATH the service will use;
  • Docker running, with a Linux VM;
  • the VM's size: at least the CPUs each job gets, and at least slots × the memory each job gets, with 10% slack (Docker Desktop's "8 GB" VM reports 7.7 GB);
  • the runner image for the installed runner version.

A fix: line names Docker Desktop's setting (Settings → Resources → Advanced, then Apply & restart), and the other ways out: fewer slots, or less memory per job.

Option Meaning --slots N, --cpus N, --memory GB stand in for the pool's settings, for a "what if". Defaults: the pool's slots, and 2 CPUs and 2 GB per job

A value out of range is refused with its flag's name and range (--cpus must be from 1 to 64).

docker runs as it will in the service, with launchd's environment and the service's PATH. A shell's DOCKER_HOST, DOCKER_CONTEXT or DOCKER_CONFIG doesn't count: pick the Docker context the service should use with docker context use.

In container mode, doctor also asks Docker:

  • Docker down is exit 3, with "start Docker Desktop" as the next step.
  • A VM too small for the slots is a warning.
  • A running pool whose jobs still run on the Mac or reach its own services is a warning (the container checks in the doctor list above); restart it then.

docs.title: Repo scripts (working on the template)
docs.text:
scripts/check.sh [-j N] [repo-path] in the amplifactory repo (not shipped to generated projects) is the local "checks pass". Options go before the repo path; anything after it is an error.

What it does:

  1. Reads the Template CI variants and render steps from .github/workflows/template-ci.yml (the file GitHub runs).
  2. Renders each variant with --vcs-ref HEAD (commit first), in parallel: one job per variant, capped by the CPU count. -j N or CHECK_JOBS=N runs them in batches of N; -j 1 runs them one at a time. Each batch's results print as soon as it finishes, in the matrix order.
  3. Runs each step with bash -eo pipefail (the first failing command fails the step).
  4. Runs the version check (VERSION vs the first CHANGELOG bullet).

Behavior:

  • It exits non-zero on any failure and warns when the tree is dirty.
  • It keeps its temp dir (printing the path) only on failure. Ctrl-C stops the running renders and their children, and keeps the temp dir.
  • scripts/test-check.sh tests it against fake repos in a few seconds; run it when you change check.sh.
  • Template CI runs both: job check-sh, shown as "scripts/check.sh's tests", and on macOS again under /bin/bash (bash 3.2). It runs whenever Template CI does (every pull request, drafts included, and pushes to main).

See the root CLAUDE.md for the full definition, including the skill scripts' --self-test runs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Copier generates an old version of the template

Copier renders the latest tag, not your working tree. Tag a release, or pass --vcs-ref HEAD while developing the template.

bootstrap.sh skips the Project board

Your gh login lacks the project scope. Run gh auth refresh -h github.com -s project and re-run the script.

The ruleset isn't enforced

On GitHub Free, rulesets don't apply to private repos. Make the repo public or use GitHub Pro. EMU (enterprise-managed) accounts can only create private repos.

bootstrap.sh --public fails on a work account

EMU (enterprise-managed) accounts can't create public repos. Re-run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh --private: the script is safe to re-run.

The repo has no factory-*.yml workflows

It was generated with actions_agent: none, the default, so the factory runs from the skill. To add the Actions mode, run uvx copier update --data actions_agent=copilot (or =claude) in a PR of its own. With copilot, then run the command the update prints, which lets workflows open pull requests.

An Actions stage didn't run on a PR

A PR that changes a workflow skips that workflow's stage. Merge workflow changes in their own PR, then click Update branch on the open PRs: PR runs use the merge ref from their last update.

Actions mode with Copilot: a build PR shows workflows awaiting approval

GitHub holds the runs of a PR the workflow token opens until someone approves them, and factory-build's approve-runs job approves them. If that job failed or didn't run, or warned that runs were still appearing after 3 minutes, click Approve workflows to run on the PR.

Only those runs count as the PR's required checks: a CI run you start with gh workflow run doesn't.

Actions mode with Copilot: the design job, or the build's approve-runs job, fails with \"opened no PR\"

The agent stopped without its PR. Its log and the issue (or design PR) comments say why. If its gh pr create failed with "GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests", turn on Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests (Settings → Actions → General), or run gh api -X PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow -F can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true.

The Actions review job is green but posted nothing

PRs authored by claude[bot] need allowed_bots and the right restrict_untrusted_prs setting in the review workflow.

The factory won't merge although CI is green

Check the gates: usually an unresolved review thread (gate 11), a branch behind main (gate 2) or a change under .github/, .claude/ or CLAUDE.md (gates 6 and 8), which you merge yourself.

A lane doesn't start

queue.py shows why: waiting means a "blocked by" link to an open issue or lane, asked means a question is waiting for you. Other ready lanes only start in parallel after you allow it.

lanes.py fails with a 404 or 422

The sub-issue and dependency APIs need the issue's internal id, which lanes.py looks up for you. A 422 on sub-add usually means the issue already has a different parent: an issue can only be in one lane.

python: command not found

The skill's scripts run as python3: stock macOS has no python. Use python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/..., and make sure Python 3.9 or newer is installed.

The Documentation tech-debt issue is missing

Repos bootstrapped before v0.6.0 don't have it, and a bootstrap that stopped early may not have created it. python3 .claude/skills/factory/scripts/lanes.py doc-debt find prints its number and creates it if missing.

sync.py prints refused: …

A guard fired. Unless the message says otherwise, nothing was written. The common ones:

  • working tree is not clean: commit or stash, then rerun.
  • branch local/adopt-<tag> already exists (locally or on origin): an earlier sync left it. Continue on it, or delete it and rerun.
  • the skill folders differ from <tag> (items modified:, missing locally:, untracked:, only local:): your local copy no longer matches the tag it claims. Restore the files from that tag, or move your own changes out, then rerun.
  • diff -rq after apply failed (items differs:, extra:): files were written but don't match the tag. Run the undo command the message prints, then report it.
  • <tag> is not an annotated tag: use a real vX.Y.Z release tag.
  • _src_path … is not … on GitHub (a local clone or a fork?): copier-check wants _src_path: gh:rahmansunny071/amplifactory in .copier-answers.yml (edit the existing line, don't add a second). The old repo name is also accepted.
  • this is amplifactory itself (or a fork of it): the sync never runs in the template repo.
Actions mode with Claude: /install-github-app fails with a workflow-scope error

The installer pushes workflow files, which needs the workflow scope on your gh login. Run gh auth refresh -h github.com -s repo,workflow, then run /install-github-app again.

CI jobs wait forever (Queued) on a repo that uses the runner pool

Run python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py doctor --repo OWNER/REPO and python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/runners.py status.

  • Container mode and Docker isn't running (doctor or status shows a docker: line; the pool also looks down): start Docker Desktop, or setup.py container off --yes. Skip the next bullet.
  • Pool down (exit code 3, no heartbeat for 2 minutes): python3 .claude/skills/factory-ci/scripts/setup.py service install --yes restarts it, once the runner is installed (runners.py base --install).
  • Paused: runners.py resume.
  • Repo not registered, or FACTORY_RUNNER not local: setup.py apply register --repo OWNER/REPO, then setup.py apply route --repo OWNER/REPO --yes.
  • PR from a fork: it never runs on the pool.
  • Draft PR: CI skips drafts; mark it ready.
